lesson_intent.one_sentence_goal: Practice wh-questions for basic personal and workday information.
lesson_intent.real_life_context: A friendly office conversation with a new colleague.
lesson_intent.communicative_function: Asking where, what, when, and how questions.

dialogue_task.scenario: Anna asks Erik simple questions about where he lives, when he starts, and what he does after work, and Erik asks some questions back.

main_focus.name: wh-questions in main clauses
main_focus.description: Use common question words followed by the verb to ask for everyday information.
main_focus.desired_presence: Use wh-questions naturally 5-6 times across the dialogue.

vocabulary_target.desired_presence: Use question words in practical, friendly questions rather than as an isolated list.

dialogue_shape.opening: One speaker greets the other and asks how things are.
dialogue_shape.middle: They ask and answer several basic wh-questions about location, time, and plans after work.
dialogue_shape.ending: They close with a friendly comment about the day.

target_complexity.repetition: repeat the wh-question pattern with varied question words

focus: when a speaker starts or finishes
what a speaker plans after work
